**The meaning of the hadith**
The right of a Muslim over his Muslim brother is great, and only a believer of strong faith and noble character fulfils this right. The Prophet ﷺ used to train people to fulfil the rights of brotherhood among themselves, so that society would be loving and cooperative, and people would enjoy a good life in this world and be happy in the Hereafter with an abundant reward from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

In this hadith the Prophet ﷺ commands three things, all of which are among the rights of a Muslim over a Muslim; … and he commanded freeing the 'ani, and the 'ani is the captive. So one must strive to free him and release him from captivity by every available means, whether with money or otherwise.

When people fulfil such rights towards one another, they increase friendship and affection, and remove grudges and resentment from hearts and souls.

📖 From the Hadith Encyclopedia — Dorar.net.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did Sheikh Bashir say that freeing Murad was a right over all the Muslims, not only over his own family?
2. Everyone in the village helped with what they had. What did the fisherman who had no money give? And what did Yasin give, and why did he say, "And that is my father — and his brothers who are with him"?
3. How did Murad and the others get out of prison? (Through the truth, not by force: the trustworthy men testified before the judge to what they had seen, and he found the real thief. Helping someone who has been wronged is done in lawful ways.)

**This week's exercise**
Choose together one of the three deeds in the hadith, and complete it before the end of the week: food that your child carries to someone who needs it, a visit to a sick relative or a phone call to them, or part of their pocket money that they put with their own hand into charity for a family in need.
